correctness.rationale: For diagonal |λ_j|=1, any midpoint representation U=(X+Y)/2 in numerical-radius unit ball compresses to every two-coordinate plane. At a numerical-radius-one diagonal unitary D, saturated diagonal states imply all diagonal perturbations vanish; PSD of I−Re(conjugate(λ_j)(D±A)) forces A_21=−λ_j² conjugate(A_12) and A_12=−λ_k² conjugate(A_21); unless λ_k=−λ_j, off-diagonal entries vanish (equal λ case by polarization). An exact antipodal pair admits square-zero norm-two matrices W±=diag(1,−1)±[[0,i],[i,0]], w(W±)=1 and nontrivial midpoint. Therefore diagonal extreme iff no exact antipodes. For nearly antipodal pairs δ_n=|λ_j+λ_k|→0, the corresponding H_n with 2×2 block λ_j[[0,i],[i,0]] has w(H_n)=1 and w(U±H_n)≤1+δ_n; X_n,Y_n normalized by 1+δ_n have midpoint error δ_n/(1+δ_n)→0 and distance 2/(1+δ_n)→2, maximally permitted by triangle inequality. Example diag(1,−exp(i/(n+2))) blocks meets both spectral conditions. Independent finite angular tests show lower diameter→2; infinite statement follows from matrix compression and δ_n→0.
